[risk] Read-only: nothing is modified.

maxItems.description: Stop after this many instances (default 500, hard cap 5000). Lower it to keep the response small.

tools.name: spatial_map
tools.description:
3D occupancy grid over a region. Returns cells [{x,y,z,occupied,parts:[InstancePath],terrainSolid,terrainMaterial}] plus stats {parts, collisions, air}. region accepts {min:[x,y,z], max:[x,y,z]}, a 6-number array [minX,minY,minZ,maxX,maxY,maxZ], or a 12-number CFrame array plus size:[x,y,z]. cellSize is in studs (default 4); large regions are capped to keep Studio responsive. Without region the map is empty — always pass a region. The per-cell list dominates the payload in big regions: pass summaryOnly:true when you only need stats.

[risk] Read-only: nothing is modified.

region.description: Region to map. Accepts {min:[x,y,z], max:[x,y,z]}, a 6-number array [minX,minY,minZ,maxX,maxY,maxZ], or a 12-number CFrame array together with size:[x,y,z] (box centered on the CFrame position). Without region the map is empty.

cellSize.description: Cell edge in studs (default 4). Total cells are capped (default 20000); raise cellSize for big regions.

includeTerrain.description: Also mark terrainSolid/terrainMaterial per cell (one voxel read for the whole region).

summaryOnly.description: Omit the per-cell list and return only stats/dimensions/region. Use it when you need the counts (or the region is large) and not the cells.

size.description: Box size [x,y,z]; only used together with a 12-number CFrame region.

inputSchema.description: 3D occupancy grid over a region. Returns cells [{x,y,z,occupied,parts:[InstancePath],terrainSolid,terrainMaterial}] plus stats {parts, collisions, air}. region accepts {min:[x,y,z], max:[x,y,z]}, a 6-number array [minX,minY,minZ,maxX,maxY,maxZ], or a 12-number CFrame array plus size:[x,y,z]. cellSize is in studs (default 4); large regions are capped to keep Studio responsive. Without region the map is empty — always pass a region. The per-cell list dominates the payload in big regions: pass summaryOnly:true when you only need stats.

tools.name: measure
tools.description:
Measure a set of instances. mode 'distance' = straight-line studs between the first two paths (uses their bounding-box center, so Models work); 'bounds' = per-instance spatial readout {position, size, rotationDeg, look/up, min/max/bottomY/topY} (where it is, how big, how tall, how rotated); 'gap' = spatial relation between the first two paths: signed gap per axis (positive = separated, negative = overlap depth), intersect, surfaceDistance, rotation deltas, whether A's footprint fits inside B, and suggestedMove to bring the faces together — pass aAt:[x,y,z] to test a candidate position; 'volume' = summed part volumes; 'extents' = aggregated world bounding box (center, size, min, max) over all given instances, Models included; 'count' = how many paths resolved. A path that does not resolve is an error, never a silent skip. Use 'bounds' + 'gap' to place objects without iterating blind.

[risk] Read-only: nothing is modified.

aAt.description: Only for mode 'gap': pretend the first path (A) is at this [x,y,z] before measuring, to test a candidate placement without moving anything. The reported gaps/move are relative to A's would-be position.

inputSchema.description: Measure a set of instances. mode 'distance' = straight-line studs between the first two paths (uses their bounding-box center, so Models work); 'bounds' = per-instance spatial readout {position, size, rotationDeg, look/up, min/max/bottomY/topY} (where it is, how big, how tall, how rotated); 'gap' = spatial relation between the first two paths: signed gap per axis (positive = separated, negative = overlap depth), intersect, surfaceDistance, rotation deltas, whether A's footprint fits inside B, and suggestedMove to bring the faces together — pass aAt:[x,y,z] to test a candidate position; 'volume' = summed part volumes; 'extents' = aggregated world bounding box (center, size, min, max) over all given instances, Models included; 'count' = how many paths resolved. A path that does not resolve is an error, never a silent skip. Use 'bounds' + 'gap' to place objects without iterating blind.

tools.name: raycast
tools.description:
Cast one ray inside Workspace from origin toward direction (or target) up to maxDistance. Returns {hit, distance, position, normal, instance, className, material}; hit:false with distance=maxDistance when nothing is in the way. Read-only. Use it to check 'what is below this part', ground/height under an object, or whether A can see/touch B, without ad-hoc execute_luau. ignorePaths excludes the parts you are placing (terrain is still hit unless a path to it is ignored).

[risk] Read-only: casts a ray and reports the hit; nothing is modified.

direction.description: Ray direction [x,y,z] (not required to be normalized). Provide this or target.

target.description: Point to aim at [x,y,z]; the direction is computed from origin. Provide this or direction.

maxDistance.description: How far the ray travels in studs (default 1000).

ignorePaths.description: Instances (and their descendants) the ray ignores, e.g. the part you are about to place. A path that does not resolve is an error.

ignore.description: Alias of ignorePaths, accepted for convenience. Prefer ignorePaths.

inputSchema.description: Cast one ray inside Workspace from origin toward direction (or target) up to maxDistance. Returns {hit, distance, position, normal, instance, className, material}; hit:false with distance=maxDistance when nothing is in the way. Read-only. Use it to check 'what is below this part', ground/height under an object, or whether A can see/touch B, without ad-hoc execute_luau. ignorePaths excludes the parts you are placing (terrain is still hit unless a path to it is ignored).

tools.name: create_instance

On failure nothing is left behind (created instance is destroyed). Records an undo waypoint.

[risk] Low. Leaves an undo waypoint (Ctrl+Z).

[risk] Low. Leaves an undo waypoint (Ctrl+Z). Creates or moves a piece adjacent to a reference face.

tools.name: csg_operation
tools.description:
CSG boolean operation (union, subtract, intersect) on 2 or more BaseParts, using Studio's own async CSG (BasePart:UnionAsync/SubtractAsync/IntersectAsync): all parts are combined in one operation, in the order given. Creates the resulting part, and with keepOriginals:false (default) the source parts are destroyed ONLY after the result is in the tree, so a failure leaves every source part intact. Records an undo waypoint.

[risk] Medium. Leaves an undo waypoint (Ctrl+Z). CSG boolean op destroys source parts unless keepOriginals:true.

tools.name: transform
tools.description:

BaseParts accept cframe (12 numbers, position first: x,y,z,R00..R22), position (3 numbers), rotation or size; Models accept position/cframe and are moved whole with PivotTo (rotation preserved). Non-spatial classes (Folder, Script, services) are rejected. Grid snapping uses StudioService.GridSize unless snap:false. Records an undo waypoint.

[risk] Medium. Leaves an undo waypoint (Ctrl+Z).

tools.name: batch_transaction
tools.description:
Apply a list of operations in ONE command (one round trip, one Ctrl+Z) instead of N separate calls. The whole batch is validated first (op names, required args, paths): a batch with a bad op applies NOTHING and answers applied:0. After that it is still NOT atomic: operations run in order and it stops at the first failure, reporting results[] per operation and how many were applied (what was applied stays applied). op is one of create (create_instance args), set_properties, transform, delete, clone, rename, reparent, group; args is the same object that op's own tool takes (dryRun is honored per operation). Use it for bulk building: hundreds of parts in one call.

[risk] Medium-High. The whole batch is validated first (op names, required args, paths), so a batch with a bad op applies nothing; after that it is still NOT atomic: it applies the operations in order and STOPS at the first failure, so what was already applied stays. A partial batch is still one Ctrl+Z. Read results[] to see which operation failed.

inputSchema.description: Apply a list of operations in ONE command (one round trip, one Ctrl+Z) instead of N separate calls. The whole batch is validated first (op names, required args, paths): a batch with a bad op applies NOTHING and answers applied:0. Use it for bulk building: hundreds of parts in one call.

tools.name: terrain_fill

Fill terrain: shape 'block' (cframe+size), 'ball' (cframe+radius), 'cylinder' (cframe+height+radius), 'region' (region), 'wedge'. 'block' and 'region' give hard 4-stud steps; for organic shapes prefer 'ball'/'cylinder'/'wedge', and for smooth slopes/hills use terrain_write_voxels with fractional occupancy. Use dryRun:true first for a cell estimate; region volume is capped at 4,000,000 studs^3. Cleared/filled terrain is NOT auto-restorable — refill the same region to undo. Records an undo waypoint.

[risk] High. Cleared/filled terrain is NOT auto-restorable (refill the same region to recover). dryRun:true previews the cell count. Leaves an undo waypoint (Ctrl+Z) for the fill itself.

cframe.description: 12 numbers in CFrame.new order: x, y, z, R00, R01, R02, R10, R11, R12, R20, R21, R22. POSITION FIRST, then the 9 rotation-matrix components (identity = [x,y,z, 1,0,0, 0,1,0, 0,0,1]).

tools.name: terrain_write_voxels
tools.description:
Write terrain materials/occupancy in a region (arrays paralleling the 4-stud grid). occupancy accepts FRACTIONAL values 0..1, not just 0/1: the engine interpolates the surface inside and between voxels, so a solid body (1) with a partially-filled top cell (e.g. height mod 4 / 4) gives smooth, non-blocky terrain, while plain 0/1 occupancy gives stair-steps at 4 studs. Keep every value within 0..1. Materials are still assigned per voxel, but the engine blends the transition between different materials, so material boundaries read as gradients rather than hard 4-stud lines. Arrays are 3D and grow with the region: keep regions modest (large ones are heavy to send) and dryRun first. Same volume cap and no auto-restore caveats as terrain_fill.

[risk] High. Same terrain caveats as terrain_fill: not auto-restorable, dryRun first, waypoint for the write.

inputSchema.description: Write terrain materials/occupancy in a region (arrays paralleling the 4-stud grid). occupancy accepts FRACTIONAL values 0..1, not just 0/1: the engine interpolates the surface inside and between voxels, so a solid body (1) with a partially-filled top cell (e.g. height mod 4 / 4) gives smooth, non-blocky terrain, while plain 0/1 occupancy gives stair-steps at 4 studs. Keep every value within 0..1. Materials are still assigned per voxel, but the engine blends the transition between different materials, so material boundaries read as gradients rather than hard 4-stud lines. Arrays are 3D and grow with the region: keep regions modest (large ones are heavy to send) and dryRun first. Same volume cap and no auto-restore caveats as terrain_fill.

tools.name: create_script
tools.description:
Create a Script/LocalScript/ModuleScript with source under a parent. class accepts 'className' as an alias. Syntax is validated with loadstring when available (otherwise the response says syntaxValidated:false). CAUTION: creating then editing a script leaves NO usable undo waypoint — a single Ctrl+Z can remove the whole script.

[risk] Medium. WARNING: creating AND editing a script leaves NO usable undo waypoint — a single Ctrl+Z can remove the whole script (the script editor keeps its own undo stack).

tools.name: get_script_source
tools.description:
Read a script's source. Without a range the whole source is returned; with startLine/endLine (or snake_case start_line/end_line, also accepted) only those lines are returned, numbered, and the full source is omitted to save tokens. Ranges are 1-based and inclusive; invalid ranges are rejected.

[risk] Read-only: nothing is modified.

startLine.description: First line to return (1-based, inclusive). Requires endLine.

endLine.description: Last line to return (1-based, inclusive). Requires startLine.

inputSchema.description: Read a script's source. tools.name: set_script_source
tools.description:
Replace a script's source. Syntax validated with loadstring when available. CAUTION: Ctrl+Z afterwards can delete the entire script. Studio's undo recording is opened and committed, but it captures nothing for a source change, so undo hits the PREVIOUS waypoint — for a script MCP just created, that waypoint is its creation (measured: one Ctrl+Z removed the script). Prefer multi_edit (native) for edits.

[risk] High. WARNING: Studio's undo recording is opened and committed but captures nothing for a source change, so Ctrl+Z afterwards hits the previous waypoint — for a script MCP just created, that deletes the entire script. Prefer multi_edit (native) for edits.

tools.name: list_scripts
tools.description:
List scripts with metadata (path, ClassName, name, Enabled, source length). root defaults to the whole place; classFilter narrows to Script/LocalScript/ModuleScript. Scripts that belong to generated ProceduralModels are counted separately (proceduralDependencies) and excluded from the main list unless includeProceduralDependencies:true.

[risk] Read-only: nothing is modified.

includeProceduralDependencies.description: Include the ModuleScripts generated inside ProceduralModels (excluded by default; they are model dependencies, not game scripts).
